newsitem.title: USA: FAA probes "near miss" of jets over Los Angeles.
newsitem.headline: FAA probes "near miss" of jets over Los Angeles.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration said on Thursday it was investigating why two passenger jets came within 300 feet (100 metres) of each other over Los Angeles this week.

An FAA spokesman said the two planes, a Boeing 747 of the Dutch national airline KLM and an MD-11 belonging to the Brazilian airline VASP, had a "near miss" while approaching Los Angeles International Airport on Wednesday afternoon.
He said the VASP plane veered in front of the KLM jet and failed to turn away as directed by air traffic controllers.
The Dutch plane's pilot had to take evasive action, he said, adding that the FAA was investigating the incident which he referred to as "pilot deviation."
Both planes landed without further incident and no one was injured.
